title: Rolling cannot erase the cloth
hook: With no compressed air, which uses less cloth volume?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that rolling or folding removes no cloth, so the clothes' own volume is the same either way; any space saved comes from squeezing out air and filling gaps

misconception: Rolling clothes makes them take less space than folding them.
objective: Changing shape does not remove material. This ideal sheet has the same volume rolled or folded. Real space differences come from air gaps, compression and how shapes share a bag.

claims.text: Changing shape does not remove material: the cloth's volume is the same rolled or folded. Real differences come from air gaps, compression and how the shapes share the bag.
claims.source: Recall transfer item for this lesson; scenario values are stipulated in the question. The why applies the lesson's own model and limits (see this lesson's idea, limit and formula claims). Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Derivation: engine case conserve gives material volume = count × 30 × 20 × 0.2 = count × 120 cm³ for both Fold and Roll (value does not depend on the layout flag). The space an item takes in a bag is its material volume plus enclosed air, shaped by how it packs with its neighbours, so a real difference must come from air gaps, compression (removing air) or the packing arrangement, which is the list given. Keyed option (index 2, "Less trapped air, or more squeezing") is the only one consistent with this; the others contradict conservation or speak of weight.

recall.question: Your rolled shirts take less room in the bag than folded ones. Using the lesson, where did the saving come from?
options: Rolling shrank the amount of cloth itself
Less trapped air, or more squeezing
recall.why: Changing shape does not remove material: the cloth's volume is the same rolled or folded. Real differences come from air gaps, compression and how the shapes share the bag.
